## Source: amazon-inspector (88c47b01a7b3719e60ecd10a1293f60f948c8c68e22e308caa161c0ed732a416)
juyip-parser-assets@1.0.1 advertises itself as a compressed-asset storage helper, but its saveAsset function contains an undocumented side effect unrelated to compression: on every invocation, it checks whether a file named '../ls' exists relative to the process working directory and, if so, calls fs.chmodSync('../ls', 0o755) to mark it executable. The target path is outside the package's own directory, the filename mimics a common system utility, and the operation has no connection to the stated compressed-asset purpose. This is the executable-bit-flipping half of a split-package dropper pattern: a companion component stages a binary at that path and this package silently makes it runnable on the installer's host whenever the library's advertised API is used.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
